_note: Our own writing. The situation at a hub: two sides in tension, with the squad in between (patterns from the core book's setting, Core p.10-11, p.21, p.126, and from published campaigns: see docs/research/lancer_campaigns.md). Side A is the hub's own faction; side B is a generated outside faction. Helping one side costs standing with the other (our bookkeeping, see src/story/README.md). Hooks are the job templates each side tends to offer.

summary: {b} holds the charter for {planet}, and the colonists of {hub} say it's squeezing them dry.
{b} wants the land around {hub} for a new project. The people living on it disagree.
{b} has more security in {hub} than the local government has police. Everyone's waiting to see who blinks first.
The governor of {hub} signed a deal with {b}. Half the town thinks it was a sellout.
Raiders have been hitting every convoy out of {hub}. {b} takes a cut of everything that moves.
The trade lanes around {planet} are bleeding cargo, and {b} is getting rich.

conflicts.a_role: those who want to rejoin the wider galaxy
summary: {planet} was cut off for generations. Now that the gates are open, {hub} is split down the middle about what comes next.
{b} says outsiders bring nothing but debt and guns. They might not be entirely wrong.
Two houses claim {hub}, and both have hired lancers. Nobody says 'war' out loud yet.
{b} wants a duel, a marriage or a massacre. It hasn't decided which.
{b} has been hitting {hub_faction} targets for months. Some call them terrorists, some call them the only ones fighting back.
The roads out of {hub} are checkpoints now. {b} owns the night.
Something valuable came down near {hub}, and everyone with a mech wants a piece of it.
{b} has been jumping salvage claims all season. The claim-holders want it stopped.
